correctness.rationale: Proof establishes the vertex characterization from binary incidence extremality, sharp 2n upper bound, a bijective two-state scan with exact V and H transitions, k-dependent degree formula, weighted Fibonacci recurrence and asymptotic. Exhaustive checks of every vertex pair for n=2..12 and all tile-transfer cases for n=2..19 corroborate. Finite tests are not offered as an infinite proof.

evidence: Torres proves a general k-matching polytope normality and linear description, not a Euclidean diameter-pair theorem.
The inspected total-matching polytope result works with selected vertices and edges of complete bipartite K_{p,q} in R^(p+q+pq), versus perfect matchings of an open ladder in R^(3n-2).
A general upper bound 2n from fixed matching size does not imply its attainment, let alone counts and degrees.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Even though the matching-polytope construction is a specialization of general k-matching polytopes, the existing structural H-description/normality does not imply metric extremal multiplicities. Likewise the total-matching theorem cannot be specialized by parameter substitution to this sparse-graph face or edge-only metric.

value.rationale: A natural classical infinite family of perfect-matching polytopes has a complete exact Euclidean longest-chord graph degree spectrum, including placement invariance, parity-isolated vertex, and an explicit exponentially sparse set of diametral pairs. The object and metric are mathematically canonical and the result is not a relabeling of graph flip-distance or the Fibonacci vertex count.
